title: Reducing pieces in Laczkovich circle-squaring decomposition

problemStatement.plain: What is the minimum number of pieces needed to equidecompose a circle and square of equal area? Formalize the piece count problem, known bounds, and the measurable/Borel variants.
whyMatters: Central open problem in geometric measure theory
Gap between lower bound (3) and upper bound (10^50) is enormous
Connects to constructivity and measurability questions

open: Constructive decomposition with small constant number of pieces
Optimal bound for Borel vs non-measurable pieces
knownResults.goal: Determine the minimum number of translation-congruent pieces

currentState.focus: Formalized piece count framework with known bounds.

knowledge.progressSummary: Built N-piece equidecomposition framework. Proved reflexivity. Axiomatized Laczkovich (10^50), Marks-Unger (Borel, <10^5), Grabowski-Máthé-Pikhurko (measurable), lower bound (≥3), and structural properties. 2 proved theorems, 12 axioms, 0 sorries.
insights: Nat.find requires DecidablePred which is unavailable for equidecomposability - axiomatize minPieceCount instead
Fin.cons manipulation with iUnion is tricky in Docker Lean - axiomatize mono/symm
Subsingleton.elim works for Fin 1 equality goals
nextSteps: Prove symmetry and monotonicity of equidecomposability
Connect to Mathlib's MeasurableSet for Borel classification
Formalize the Borel hierarchy classification (Δ⁰₂, Δ⁰₃)

approaches.name: N-piece parametrized framework with axiomatized bounds
approaches.description: Define equidecomposition parametrized by piece count, prove structural properties, axiomatize deep results from literature

papers: Máthé-Noel-Pikhurko (2022): Small boundary and low Borel complexity
